question: How does contrastive learning differ from standard supervised classification?
direct_answer: It learns representations by comparing examples rather than predicting fixed class labels.
expanded_answer: Supervised classification uses human labels and trains the model to output a class. Contrastive learning usually uses pairwise similarity: it asks whether two examples should be close or far in representation space. That makes contrastive learning especially useful when labels are unavailable or when the goal is to learn general-purpose embeddings rather than a task-specific classifier.
key_points: Uses similarity relations, not class IDs
common_wrong_ideas: It is just classification with a different loss
It cannot use any supervision at all
It only works for image tasks
